continuity.narrative_arc: Kamsa dispatches his devotee Akrura to fetch Krishna; Akrura travels in joyful inward prayer, recognizes Vrindavana’s sanctity, reaches the evening milking courtyard, meets the youthful brothers, is welcomed by Nanda and Krishna, and the stanza closes with the gopikas’ uncertainty and Bhattathiri’s prayer.
continuity.krishna_identity: Use the shared krishna-vrindavan-youth contract: deep matte indigo-blue skin; serene youthful cowherd face; dark wavy hair; yellow dhoti; muted red-orange shawl; single low gold band and one upright peacock feather; plain smooth forehead with no mark; ordinary two-arm/two-leg anatomy. Identity refs guide face only, not pose or scene.
continuity.akrura_contract: Akrura is Krishna’s devotee, not a villain. Use the chapter-scoped mature devotee contract: warm-brown skin, simple travel clothes, natural anatomy, humble and joyful demeanor.
continuity.balarama_contract: Use the chapter-scoped Vrindavan-youth contract, distinct from the shared toddler-stage Balarama entry: youthfully proportioned elder brother, natural warm light-brown skin, restrained blue garment, ordinary two-arm/two-leg anatomy.
continuity.supporting_cast_contract: Use shared Nandagopan, gopas and gopikas contracts. Nanda is a mature moustached householder in cream/olive; gopikas are distinct, fully clothed women; gopas are a small distinct group. Stanza 12 uses shared clean-shaven older Bhattathiri and approved Guruvayurappan identity cues only.
continuity.palette_arc: Traditional matte South Indian temple mural; firm dark contours, flat mineral fields, ochre, cream, deep maroon, muted olive and deep indigo-blue. Warm-brown human skin stays clearly brown (red-minus-blue under about 120); Krishna’s skin stays deep indigo (blue-minus-red at least 40). No gloss, metallic gold, border, beams or readable text.
